en.title: Longest Non-Decreasing Run After One Change
en.description:
You may change at most one element of the array to any integer. Output the length of the longest contiguous non-decreasing subarray after the change. Non-decreasing allows equal values.

The standard input/output, examples, and tests are written by CSWork; ranges marked "this site" are judging conventions and are not claimed to be original interview limits.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000); the second line contains n integers (−10⁹..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer as described; results for multiple queries are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: Example 1: change 0 to 8, and the whole array becomes non-decreasing, with length 6. Example 2: change the first element 3 to 2 to get a non-decreasing run of length 2; a single change cannot make 3, 2, 1 entirely non-decreasing. Example 3: a single element is by itself a run of length 1.
hints: Compute the lengths of the unmodified non-decreasing runs ending at and starting at each position. When changing one position, consider extending only the left run, only the right run, and merging the two runs when the neighboring values on both sides allow a bridge.
